title: GIS Support Specialist — permanent, agency-wide geospatial application
org: Wyoming Game and Fish Department · Cheyenne, WY
benefits: State of Wyoming employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Closes Aug 13 · ~$73,000–$81,000 · PERMANENT benefited GIS career post · bachelor's preferred
body: A permanent benefited position leading technical administration and support of an agency-wide geospatial compliance application, serving as liaison to habitat biologists and regulatory applicants, and helping design future enterprise GIS applications. A bachelor's degree is preferred, and the posting stresses communication and user support as much as raw technical GIS skill.
desc: This is a permanent GIS career position inside a state wildlife agency at a salary well above anything else found this run at her level — and the posting's emphasis on communication and user support plays to a strength that technical postings usually ignore. Her multi-criteria suitability modelling is the qualifying credential.

title: Hydrographer Commissioner — stream gaging and water measurement
org: Wyoming State Engineer's Office · Big Piney, WY
benefits: State of Wyoming employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Rolling · $32.33–$35.92/hr · PERMANENT · minimum is a science BS with 0–3 years
body: A permanent full-time position measuring, monitoring and regulating water supplies across a state water division: daily water-use accounting, data analysis, facility and reservoir inspections, dam-safety checks, installing stream gaging equipment, and mediating disputes among water users. The minimum qualification is a bachelor's degree in the sciences with zero to three years of experience.
desc: A permanent state water-resources job whose stated minimum is a science bachelor's with as little as zero years of experience, paying over $32 an hour. Installing and reading stream gages is hands-on watershed work, and water-rights administration is a specialised credential that is genuinely hard to get into from outside.

body: A part-time, irregular-hours research technician supporting the water programmes of a San Juan Mountains research non-profit, with a start as early as August 17, 2026 and work through approximately March 2027. The amount of work and the end date are contingent on project needs and the schedule is flexible. Reports to the Director of Water Programs.
desc: The San Juans are heavily mining-affected country, which makes this the closest thematic match to her Pigeon River trace-metal capstone found anywhere this run — same question, different mountains. The catch is honest: it is part-time with irregular hours, so it works best stacked alongside something else rather than as a sole income.

title: GIS Technician — wildlife geospatial layers and mobile data apps
org: Wyoming Game and Fish Department · Cheyenne, WY
benefits: Contract full-time — confirm the benefit package with the department
metaLine: Closes Aug 27 · $27.39/hr · ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online production work for state biologists
body: A contract full-time role updating and standardising wildlife-related GIS layers, interpreting boundary descriptions to create spatial features, verifying geometry and metadata, producing maps, and building web maps and mobile data-collection apps. The position provides GIS support to department biologists. Preference is for a bachelor's in GIS, geography or a related field with ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online experience.
desc: Straight ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online production work at a state wildlife agency, which is a cleaner use of her GIS training than most field roles that treat mapping as an afterthought. Building mobile data-collection apps is also a genuinely transferable skill worth having on a resume.

title: Surface Water Professional — permanent water-rights review
org: Wyoming State Engineer's Office · Cheyenne, WY
benefits: State of Wyoming employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Rolling · ~$67,000–$75,000 · PERMANENT benefited · minimum is a science bachelor's degree
body: A permanent benefited position reviewing surface-water permit applications, maps and water-rights petitions for compliance with Wyoming water law, resolving discrepancies with applicants, and supporting the public and other agencies on surface-water matters. The minimum qualification is a bachelor's degree, typically in the sciences.
desc: A permanent state water-resources career position at roughly $67,000 to $75,000 whose stated minimum is simply a science bachelor's degree. Reviewing permit maps also uses her GIS literacy directly, and western water law is a specialisation that compounds in value over a career.

title: Elk Feedground CWD Technician
org: Wyoming Game and Fish Department · Pinedale, WY
location: Pinedale, Wyoming (state elk feedgrounds and winter ranges)
url_label: Wyoming NEOGOV — Elk Feedground CWD Technician 2026-01821
benefits: Six-month contract — confirm the benefit package with the department
metaLine: Closes Aug 15 · $29.75/hr — the best-paid entry wildlife technician rate found this run
body: A six-month contract position starting in October or November collecting chronic wasting disease samples from elk on state feedgrounds and winter ranges. Duties include lymph node collection from hunter-harvested and road-killed cervids, lethal removal of diseased animals, detailed record keeping, and hunter and landowner outreach. Preference is given to applicants with a bachelor's in wildlife management, range management, biology or zoology.
desc: At $29.75 an hour this is the best-paid entry-level wildlife technician rate found anywhere this run, and it explicitly prefers a bachelor's like hers with no experience minimum. Worth knowing before applying: the job includes lethal removal of diseased animals, which is standard disease-management work but not something everyone wants.

body: A full-time hourly position headquartered in the NRCS Cortez Field Office providing natural-resource technical assistance to private landowners across the Mancos district. The preferred start is September 2026, with applications reviewed on an ongoing basis and full consideration given by August 16. Benefits include a health insurance stipend and paid time off.
desc: Being physically headquartered inside an NRCS field office is the detail that matters — she has named USDA as a target, and district planners working alongside NRCS staff are the single most common route into agency employment. It is flagged as entry-level at a real salary.

title: Forestry Technician — Colorado State Forest Service open hiring pool
org: Colorado State Forest Service · Colorado State University · statewide, CO
location: Statewide, Colorado (drawn on as vacancies arise)
url_label: TAMU board — Colorado State Forest Service open pool 117560
benefits: Colorado State University employee benefits — confirm the package
metaLine: Open to Dec 31 · $45,000–$55,000 · the TECHNICIAN tier has no experience minimum · apply once, considered all year
body: A continuously open hiring pool run through Colorado State University. The Forestry Technician tier asks only for a bachelor's degree in natural resource management, or an associate degree or technical training in forestry or a related field — with no professional experience minimum, unlike the parallel Forester pool. Applications are submitted through the CSU Workday careers site and drawn on as vacancies arise statewide.
desc: The distinction between the two tiers is what makes this worth doing: the Forester pool wants experience, the Technician pool does not, so her BS qualifies her outright. Because it is an open pool she can apply once now and be considered for vacancies across Colorado for the rest of the year.

body: An ACE EPIC individual placement with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Natural Resource Program Center in Fort Collins, supporting the energy and minerals programme at roughly forty hours per week. The posting is open until filled and Public Land Corps eligible, which can confer non-competitive federal hiring eligibility. The placement sits directly alongside USFWS staff.
desc: A housing reimbursement on top of an $805 weekly allowance is unusually generous for a service placement, and Public Land Corps eligibility plus a USFWS mentor is the most direct on-ramp to the federal career she has named. Being at a national programme centre rather than a single refuge also means broader agency exposure.

title: Wildlife Technician — Individual Placement with BLM Royal Gorge Field Office
org: Southwest Conservation Corps (Conservation Legacy) with BLM · Colorado
location: Colorado (BLM Royal Gorge Field Office public lands)
stipend: AmeriCorps living allowance (amount not published on the listing — ask SCC)

metaLine: Closes Sep 1 · wildlife survey + species ID + ecological databases, embedded with BLM
body: An AmeriCorps individual placement assisting the Bureau of Land Management with wildlife research and monitoring on public lands. The member conducts field surveys of wildlife and vegetation, identifies and classifies species, records ecological data, and supports bird surveys, nest monitoring and database maintenance. A stipend plus a Segal Education Award follow completion; the minimum is age 17 and a high school diploma.
desc: Of all the corps positions found in the Mountain West this is the closest to her actual training — survey design, species identification and ecological database work rather than trail construction. She has three Conservation Legacy applications in already, so her materials transfer directly. The living allowance is not published, so ask before committing.
